title: Contract gate (mechanical stage-6) — plan 001
epic_title: Implement the mechanical stage-6 contract gate (docgate contract-gate)

tasks.title: Enrich the fold's machine face with per-requirement fields
tasks.goal: The PRD source map exposes, per requirement unit, its priority, whether it carries a fit criterion, and its declared verification method — projected additively from the already-parsed row cells — so existing consumers are unaffected.
tasks.current: The source map carries lineage fields only (status, introduced_by, supersedes, superseded_by, source_location, current_location); the row cells are parsed but never exposed on the machine face.
tasks.desired: Each requirement unit additionally carries priority (where a Priority column exists), has-fit-criterion, and verify-method, resolved by header-column name so per-table column order does not matter; re-folding an existing ledger adds the fields and changes no existing field's value.
scope: project the new fields from the parsed row cells, keyed to each table's header by column name
add the fields to the source-map schema additively; a re-fold regenerates existing projections
leave every existing machine-face field and its consumers byte-unchanged
out_of_scope: the gate's consumption of these fields (later tasks); any change to the human-face projection
acceptance: a fixture PRD's folded source map carries priority, has-fit-criterion, and verify-method per requirement, resolved by header name across the requirement tables (FR, UB, NR, NFR)
re-folding an existing ledger adds the fields and alters no existing field's value
the docgate fold and gate suites stay green — no existing consumer is perturbed
key_interfaces: the source-map unit state (additive fields); the parsed row cells and the table header columns
touches: internal/docgate/fold · internal/docgate/ledger · the source-map schema · fold golden fixtures

tasks.title: The contract-gate verb shell: resolution, verdict schema, fail-closed edges
tasks.goal: `docgate contract-gate <feature>` resolves a feature's assembled contract from the committed machine faces and returns one closed-schema verdict — clean when no check fails, and a fail-closed error or configuration-error on missing or malformed input — writing nothing.
tasks.current: docgate runs tree-wide checks and emits a defect stream; there is no feature-scoped, verdict-producing mode and no contract resolution.
tasks.desired: The verb resolves one feature's PRD projection, serving designs, and DoD; emits a closed verdict (class enum including a reserved not-evaluated semantic slot, plus the input content fingerprints and tool version); refuses fail-closed on missing or unreadable input, a malformed machine face, and an unmerged contract; makes zero mutations on any path.
scope: the verb plus feature-scoped contract resolution from the machine faces
the closed verdict schema — class enum, reserved semantic slot, fingerprint identity
the fail-closed edges before any check runs; read-only by construction
out_of_scope: the individual checks (T3, T4) — the shell runs an empty check set; the defect report (T5)
acceptance: the verb on a well-formed fixture returns a clean verdict recording the input fingerprints, with zero filesystem, git, or tracker writes
missing input yields configuration-error, a malformed machine face yields error, an unmerged contract yields configuration-error — each with zero checks run
the verdict validates closed and the reserved semantic slot is present and marked not-evaluated
key_interfaces: the contract-gate verb; the verdict schema; the contract-inputs resolver
touches: cmd/docgate · a new internal contractgate package · the verdict schema

tasks.title: The two new checks: structural completeness and compilability
tasks.goal: Two new checks, self-registered per-file with a contract-scope marker, catch structural and compilability defects: a requirement missing a fit criterion or verification method (or a missing DoD or §8) reds incomplete, and a malformed join reds malformed.
tasks.current: No structural or compilability check exists; the registry holds the tree-wide checks.
tasks.desired: The structural check reads the enriched fields and fails naming each requirement missing a fit criterion or verification method, or a missing DoD or §8; the compilability check validates the source map and Serves joins and fails naming each malformed join (orphan Serves, broken supersession, dependency cycle); both self-register from their own file carrying the contract-scope marker.
scope: the structural-completeness check over the enriched machine face
the compilability check over the source map and Serves joins
both self-registered with the contract-scope descriptor marker
out_of_scope: feature-scoping the reused checks (T4); the verb's aggregation of the subset (T2 and T4)
acceptance: seeded fixtures — a Must missing a fit criterion, one missing a verify method, a missing DoD — each red incomplete naming the requirement; a complete fixture passes
seeded fixtures — orphan Serves, dangling supersession, a dependency cycle — each red malformed naming the join; a well-formed fixture passes
each check is one new file touching no shared enumeration, dispatch, or help, and both carry the contract-scope marker
key_interfaces: the two check descriptors; the contract-scope marker field; the enriched unit state
touches: internal/docgate/gate (two new check files) · the check registry · the contract-scope marker

tasks.title: Feature-scope the three reused checks: currency, coverage, link
tasks.goal: The verb runs the three existing checks feature-scoped — currency, inverse coverage, link resolution — via verb-side unit selection, producing stale, incomplete, or unresolved verdicts scoped to one feature, with the checks' tree-wide behavior for existing callers byte-unchanged.
tasks.current: The citation, coverage, and stale-flag computations are tree-wide; nothing runs them scoped to one feature's contract or gates on them.
tasks.desired: The verb selects the feature's units from the machine faces and runs the three reused checks over that subset, marking them contract-scope; a stale serve, an uncovered Must, and a dangling citation each red the feature verdict; a feature with no live designs reds incomplete; the checks' existing tree-wide behavior for their current callers is unchanged.
scope: feature-scoped selection of the reused checks via verb-side unit selection
mark the three reused checks contract-scope; aggregate their results into the verdict
preserve each reused check's existing tree-wide behavior for its current callers
out_of_scope: the new checks (T3); changing any reused check's tree-wide logic
acceptance: seeded stale-serve reds stale, uncovered-Must reds incomplete, dangling-citation reds unresolved — each scoped to the feature and naming the offender
a feature with a PRD but no live serving designs reds incomplete (every Must unserved)
the existing docgate gate and citation verdicts on the corpus are byte-unchanged
key_interfaces: the feature-unit selector; the contract-scope subset assembly; the coverage per-feature family
touches: stale-flag readers) · the verb's subset assembly

tasks.title: The defect report: one dual-face event record
tasks.goal: On any failing verdict the verb emits exactly one structured, dual-face template-governed defect report bundling every failed check's named defects; a clean verdict emits none; the emission is read-only, so the host commits it.
tasks.desired: A bounce produces one report enumerating every failed check's defects (check id, offender, unblock) in a machine-readable face and a human rendering, governed by a template and schema; the report is emitted to a path the host reads — the gate never commits it; a clean verdict emits nothing.
scope: the dual-face report schema, template, and emitter
bundle every failed check's named defects (offender plus unblock) into one report
read-only emission to a path; nothing on a clean verdict
out_of_scope: the host's git-commit of the report (T6 and T7 own that); the report's exact home path, decided here at implementation
acceptance: a bouncing fixture emits exactly one report whose both faces validate and enumerate all failed checks with offender and unblock
a clean fixture emits zero report and zero artifact (filesystem audit)
the gate performs no git or tracker mutation while emitting (read-only audit)
key_interfaces: the defect-report schema; the report template; the read-only emitter
touches: the contractgate report emitter and template · the report schema

tasks.title: The severity-map policy and the continuous CI context
tasks.goal: The continuous advisory surface runs the contract-scope subset on PRD and design PRs with a hard-or-advisory split read from a closed-schema versioned severity-map policy — currency, link, and structural blocking, inverse-coverage advisory — with a missing policy falling back to the default split.
tasks.current: No continuous contract check and no severity-map policy exist.
tasks.desired: A closed-schema versioned severity-map policy on the pyxis-config surface encodes the per-trigger split (hard at planning entry; coverage advisory continuously); a docgate CI context runs the subset on contract-doc PRs applying it; a malformed policy fails closed with configuration-error, a missing one uses the built-in default.
scope: the closed-schema versioned severity-map policy (unknown key fails closed; missing uses the default)
the continuous CI context running the contract-scope subset with the split
coverage advisory continuously; currency, link, and structural blocking
out_of_scope: the planning-entry hard gate (T7); the checks themselves (T3/T4)
acceptance: a fixture PR seeding a currency, link, and structural defect fails the context; one whose only gap is an uncovered Must reports advisory and does not block
a malformed severity-map yields configuration-error; an absent one runs on the default split
editing the severity-map flips a fixture's hard-or-advisory outcome with zero code change
key_interfaces: the severity-map policy schema; the CI context entry; the pyxis-config surface
touches: the pyxis-config severity-map schema · the docgate CI context wiring · the workflow entry

tasks.title: The plan-new planning-entry precondition (cross-feature amendment)
tasks.goal: plan-new refuses to draft, freeze, or project a plan until `docgate contract-gate <feature>` returns clean — landed as an additive typed amendment on plan-new's own frozen ledger.
tasks.current: plan-new drafts directly from the contract with no contract-gate precondition.
tasks.desired: An additive typed amendment on plan-new's ledger introduces the precondition requirement (call the gate before drafting; refuse on any non-clean verdict, surfacing the defect report); a bouncing contract yields zero plan output and a clean one proceeds; plan-new's other ledger rows are untouched. This is a cross-feature amendment on a different feature's frozen contract — additive only.
scope: the additive typed amendment on plan-new's ledger introducing the precondition
wire plan-new to call the verb before drafting and refuse on non-clean
surface the emitted defect report to the planning session
out_of_scope: any non-additive change to plan-new's existing behavior; the continuous surface (T6)
acceptance: a bouncing contract fixture produces zero draft or plan output and surfaces the defect report; a clean one proceeds
the plan-new amendment is a single additive op and a diff shows its other ledger rows untouched
plan-new's existing fixtures stay green
key_interfaces: the plan-new precondition requirement (amendment); the verb invocation seam
touches: docs/prds/plan-new (a typed amendment on plan-new's own ledger) · the plan-new precondition call

tasks.title: Fixtures, determinism, performance, and the dogfood sweep
tasks.goal: The gate is proven deterministic, fast enough, and honest on real contracts: the fixture suite is green, the verdict is byte-identical across runs with no network, p95 wall-time is within budget on the largest live contract, and the dogfood sweep over the repo's own live contracts surfaces the known drift with zero false bounces.
tasks.current: No fixture suite, determinism and performance checks, or dogfood run exist for the gate.
tasks.desired: A fixture suite covering clean and each defect class as permanent tests; a determinism test (byte-identical verdicts; a gate network attempt fails); a performance check (p95 within the PRD's budget on the largest live contract); and a dogfood sweep running the gate over every live contract, surfacing at least the known drift instance with zero unresolved false bounces.
scope: the fixture suite (clean plus one per defect class) as permanent tests
the determinism and performance checks
the dogfood sweep over the repo's live contracts and its disposition record
out_of_scope: the LLM semantic checks (issue #419); any real second-repo onboarding
acceptance: the fixture suite is green in CI; repeated runs yield byte-identical verdicts; a gate network attempt fails the determinism suite
p95 gate wall-time is within the PRD's budget on the repo's largest live contract
the dogfood sweep surfaces at least the known drift instance with zero unresolved false bounces, with a disposition record attached
key_interfaces: the fixture corpus; the determinism and performance test harness; the dogfood sweep runner
touches: the contractgate fixture corpus · the determinism/perf tests · the dogfood sweep harness
